title: Pixel-art editor with layers, edge-connected fill, mirror drawing and palette import
prompt:
Build Pixelforge, a pixel-art editor for 16×16 game sprites. Draw the editing grid yourself (canvas or DOM); do not use a drawing or image library.

The provided sprite.json is my current sprite: copy it into the output folder next to index.html and, when nothing is saved yet, load it at runtime with fetch('sprite.json'); never hard-code its pixels. Format: width, height, a palette of hex colors, and layers listed bottom to top, each with a name, a visible flag and 16 row strings in which '.' is transparent and a digit or lowercase letter is a palette index in base 36.

Layout: a left tool rail; the editing canvas in the middle, showing each sprite pixel as a 24×24 square (384×384 in total) over a light checkerboard with thin grid lines; a right panel with the Palette, Layers, a live 4× Preview and a 'Colors used' list. A status bar shows the pixel under the pointer as 'x 5 · y 8' (0-based from the top-left) and its visible hex color.

Tools, as rail buttons with SVG icons and shortcuts: Pencil (B), Eraser (E), Fill (G), Eyedropper (I) and a Mirror toggle (M).
- Pencil paints the active color on the active layer; a drag paints every pixel along the pointer path with no gaps, even when the pointer moves fast. Eraser makes pixels transparent.
- Fill replaces the area of the clicked pixel's color that is connected through edges (not diagonals), looking only at the active layer's own pixels (transparent counts as a color). Shift+click with Fill replaces every pixel of that color on the active layer.
- Eyedropper makes the topmost visible color at a pixel the active color.
- With Mirror on, Pencil and Eraser also apply at the mirrored pixel (x becomes 15 − x).

Palette: clicking a swatch sets the active color, shown as a large chip with its hex. 'Import palette' opens a dialog to paste a GIMP .gpl palette: the first line must be 'GIMP Palette' (otherwise show 'Not a GIMP palette'); 'Name:' and 'Columns:' lines and lines starting with # are ignored; every other line is R G B as integers 0-255 separated by whitespace, optionally followed by a name. New colors are appended, colors already in the palette are skipped, bad lines are skipped, and a notice reports it like 'Imported 4 colors · 1 duplicate skipped · 2 invalid lines (lines 6, 8)' with the real counts and line numbers of the pasted text.

Layers: the list shows the top layer first, and the top layer is active on load. Each row has a visibility eye. Buttons add a layer ('Layer 4', 'Layer 5', ... inserted directly above the active layer and made active), delete, move up, move down and merge down (the active layer's opaque pixels are painted onto the layer below, which becomes active).

'Colors used' lists every color in the visible image (visible layers composited, upper layers on top) with its pixel count, most used first and ties by hex ascending, and updates after every change.

History: Ctrl+Z undoes; Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y redo (at least 50 steps). A stroke, a fill, and each layer add, delete, reorder or merge is one step; visibility toggles and palette imports are not.

'Export JSON' opens a dialog with the current sprite in the sprite.json format (lowercase hex). Pixels, palette and layers autosave to localStorage and are restored after a reload.

Visual direction: a dark, focused editor in the spirit of Aseprite: charcoal panels, crisp 1 px borders, one teal accent for the active tool and layer, compact 12-13 px labels and tabular numbers.

title: Logic circuit simulator with truth tables, loop detection and JSON import
prompt:
Build Gatewise, a digital logic circuit simulator in the browser. Write the simulator yourself; no logic or diagram library.

The provided circuit.json is my tank-controller circuit: copy it into the output folder next to index.html and, when nothing is saved yet, load it at runtime with fetch('circuit.json'); never hard-code it. It has a name, components (id, type, x, y) and wires (from a component's output to input number 0 or 1 of another component). Types: SWITCH, LED, AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NOR, XNOR.

Canvas: an SVG canvas at 1:1 scale with a 20 px grid; (x, y) is a part's top-left corner in canvas pixels. Gates are 80×60 with standard distinctive-shape symbols; two-input gates have input ports on the left edge 20 and 40 px below the top, NOT has one input in the middle, and the output port is in the middle of the right edge. Switches and LEDs are 60×40 with one port in the middle of the right edge (switch) or left edge (LED). Every part shows its name.

Editing:
- Drag a part from the left palette onto the canvas to add it; new gates take the next free number for their type (AND3, NOR1), new switches are S1, S2 and LEDs L1, L2. Dragging a part moves it; drops snap to the 20 px grid and wires follow.
- Drag from an output port to an input port to add a wire. An input takes one wire: connecting to an occupied input replaces its old wire. Click a wire or a part to select it; Delete removes it, and deleting a part also removes its wires.
- Clicking a switch toggles it between 0 and 1. Selecting a gate shows an Inspector with its name and a type dropdown; changing the type keeps the name.
- Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo every edit (add, move, wire, delete, type change, import); switch toggles are not undo steps.

Simulation is live and combinational; an unconnected input reads 0. Wires carrying 1 are green and 0 slate gray; lit LEDs glow. If wires form a cycle, a red banner reads 'Combinational loop: ' followed by the cycle in signal order starting from the part whose name sorts first and ending with it again (like 'NOR1 → XOR2 → NOR1'); the loop and everything it feeds show an amber unknown state (LEDs show '?') while the rest keeps simulating.

A status line reads like 'Components 10 · Wires 11'. A live Truth table panel has the switches in name order (the first is the most significant bit) and the LEDs in name order, rows from all 0 to all 1, and a last row with each LED's minterms like 'Σm(1,4,6)'; with a loop it shows 'Resolve the combinational loop first'.

Export shows the circuit as JSON in the circuit.json format. Import takes pasted JSON and replaces the circuit, or shows 'Invalid JSON', 'Unknown component type: <type>' or 'Unknown component in wire: <id>' and changes nothing. Autosave to localStorage and restore after a reload.

Visual direction: a clean schematic tool: off-white canvas with a dotted grid, crisp black gate outlines with NOT bubbles and the XOR double arc, wires with right-angle bends, a compact light side panel and monospaced truth-table digits.
interaction_hints: The input file is /grader/task/circuit.json; grep the page's JS for a relative fetch of circuit.json (a hard-coded circuit fails R2). Find the canvas origin with eval (getBoundingClientRect of the SVG canvas); canvas point (cx, cy) is at page origin + (cx, cy). Port positions in canvas pixels: Low output (100,100), High output (100,260), Manual output (100,420), AND1 inputs (340,140) and (340,160), OR1 output (600,190), AND2 inputs (520,360) and (520,380), AND2 body center (560,370), NOT1 body center (220,250), switch centers Low (70,100), High (70,260), Manual (70,420). Use drag with steps 15 or more; if a drag does not connect, retry with move to the start point first. Read the status line and the truth table with eval of innerText. Every scenario starts from a fresh load. (1) Screenshot; check that the NOT1 output wire is green and others gray. Click Low, screenshot (Pump lit); click High (Pump off); click Low again (Alarm lit); click Manual (Pump lit). (2) Read the truth table. (3) Click AND2's body, change its type to NAND in the Inspector (select action or eval), read the truth table and the Alarm LED with all switches off. (4) Drag from Manual's output (100,420) to AND2's second input (520,380); read the status line (wires still 11) and the Alarm column. (5) Drag from OR1's output (600,190) to AND1's first input (340,140); screenshot the banner and the Pump LED; click High and check Alarm lights; read the truth table panel; press Control+z and read the status line and truth table (Pump back to Σm(1,2,3,5,7)). (6) Click NOT1's body, press Delete, read the status line and the Pump minterms; press Control+z (NOT1 and both wires back); press Control+Shift+z. (7) Drag AND2's body from (560,370) to (597,388) and check it snaps to x 560, y 360 in Export; drag an XOR from the palette onto an empty canvas spot and read its name and the status line. (8) Import: paste {"name":"Equality","components":[{"id":"A","type":"SWITCH","x":40,"y":80},{"id":"B","type":"SWITCH","x":40,"y":200},{"id":"XNOR1","type":"FLIPFLOP","x":200,"y":120},{"id":"Same","type":"LED","x":360,"y":130}],"wires":[{"from":"A","to":"XNOR1","input":0},{"from":"B","to":"XNOR1","input":1},{"from":"XNOR1","to":"Same","input":0}]} and read the message (circuit unchanged); then paste {"name":"Equality","components":[{"id":"A","type":"SWITCH","x":40,"y":80},{"id":"B","type":"SWITCH","x":40,"y":200},{"id":"XNOR1","type":"XNOR","x":200,"y":120},{"id":"Same","type":"LED","x":360,"y":130}],"wires":[{"from":"A","to":"XNOR1","input":0},{"from":"B","to":"XNOR1","input":1},{"from":"XNOR1","to":"Same","input":0}]} and read the truth table (A, B, Same). (9) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: change AND2 to NAND, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and read the truth table again.

rubric.criterion: The layout has a part palette (Switch, LED, AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NOR, XNOR), an SVG canvas with a 20 px grid, an Inspector, a status line reading 'Components 10 · Wires 11' and a Truth table panel; gates use distinctive-shape symbols (D-shaped AND, curved OR, XOR with the extra arc, bubble on NOT).

circuit.json is in the output folder and loaded with a relative fetch; all 10 parts are drawn at their file positions with their names and the 11 wires connect the right ports; on load every switch is 0, Pump and Alarm are off, and only the wire leaving NOT1 is green.
Clicking switches simulates live: Low on lights Pump; then High on turns Pump off with Alarm off; then Low off lights Alarm; then Manual on lights Pump as well, and wire colors follow the signals.

The truth table has columns High, Low, Manual then Alarm, Pump and rows 000 to 111; Alarm is 1 only in rows 100 and 101, Pump is 1 in rows 001, 010, 011, 101 and 111, and the minterm row reads Σm(4,5) for Alarm and Σm(1,2,3,5,7) for Pump.
Changing AND2 to NAND in the Inspector keeps the name AND2, lights Alarm with all switches off, and makes Alarm's minterms Σm(0,1,2,3,6,7).
Wiring Manual's output to AND2's second input replaces the High→AND2 wire: the status line still reads 'Wires 11' and Alarm's minterms become Σm(3,5).

Wiring OR1's output to AND1's first input shows 'Combinational loop: AND1 → OR1 → AND1', Pump shows the amber unknown state, the truth table shows 'Resolve the combinational loop first', and toggling High still lights Alarm; Ctrl+Z removes the loop wire and restores Low→AND1 with Pump back to Σm(1,2,3,5,7).
Deleting NOT1 removes it with its two wires ('Components 9 · Wires 9') and Pump's minterms become Σm(1,3,5,7); Ctrl+Z restores NOT1 and both wires and Ctrl+Shift+Z deletes them again.

Dragging AND2 by about (37, 18) snaps it to x 560, y 360 with its wires following, and Export then shows that position in the circuit.json format; dragging an XOR from the palette adds 'XOR2' and 'Components 11'.

Importing JSON with a FLIPFLOP part shows 'Unknown component type: FLIPFLOP' and leaves the circuit unchanged; importing the two-switch Equality circuit replaces it, with a truth table over A, B and Same reading Σm(0,3) and 'Components 4 · Wires 3'.
After edits (for example AND2 changed to NAND), reloading the page restores the circuit and the edited truth table.

It looks like a clean schematic tool: off-white dotted grid, crisp gate outlines with NOT bubbles, tidy right-angle wires that meet the ports exactly, clear green/gray/amber signal colors, and monospaced truth-table digits in an aligned table.

title: Drum step sequencer with swing timing, song chain, Euclid fills and text import
prompt:
Build Pulse16, a 16-step drum machine with a song chain, written without audio or UI libraries.

Tracks, top to bottom: Kick, Snare, Clap, Closed hat, Open hat, Low tom, Rim, Cowbell. Each bar has 16 steps shown in four groups of four. A step is off, on or accent (drawn clearly stronger). Clicking a step turns off into on and on or accent into off; Shift+click turns off or on into accent and accent back into on.

Patterns A, B, C and D are tabs that choose the pattern being edited. Start with these (x on, X accent, . off); C and D are empty:
Pattern A: Kick X.....x...X..x.. / Snare ....X.......X... / Clap ............x... / Closed hat x.x.x.x.x.x.x.xX / Open hat ..............x. / Low tom and Cowbell empty / Rim ...x......x.....
Pattern B: Kick X.....x...X...x. / Snare ....X.......X.xx / Clap ....x.......x... / Closed hat x.x.x.x.x.x.x... / Open hat ..............X. / Low tom and Rim empty / Cowbell ..x...x...x...x.
A line above the grid reads like 'Pattern B · 22 hits · 5 accents' for the edited pattern (hits count on and accent steps).

Transport: Play/Stop (also Space), BPM (60-200, default 120) and Swing (50-75%, default 60). A sixteenth lasts T = 60 / BPM / 4 seconds; step n (1-16) starts floor((n − 1) / 2) × 2T into its bar, plus 2T × swing / 100 when n is even; bar b starts at (b − 1) × 4 × 60 / BPM. Times show as m:ss.mmm rounded to the millisecond.

Song: a chain field of pattern letters separated by spaces (default 'A A B A'; anything else shows 'Use A, B, C or D'), a timeline strip with one block per bar labeled with its pattern, and a line like 'Song: 4 bars · 0:08.000'.

Playhead: a readout like 'Bar 3 · B · Step 6 · 0:04.650' (bar, its pattern, step, time from the song start). While stopped, the period key moves one step forward and the comma key one step back through the whole chain, wrapping at both ends; Home returns to the start. The playhead column lights up in the grid when the edited pattern is the current bar's, and the current bar's block is highlighted in the timeline. Playing advances the playhead in time with the swing and loops the chain; synthesize the drum sounds with the Web Audio API.

Euclid: each track has a Euclid button with Hits k (0-16) and Rotate r (0-15): step i (0-based) is on when (i × k) mod 16 < k, then the row is rotated right by r steps; it replaces the row and clears its accents. 'Copy pattern' and 'Paste' copy the edited pattern onto another tab.

Export shows the edited pattern as text: one line per track in track order with the track name, one space and the 16 step characters. Import takes text in that format and replaces the edited pattern with its valid lines: the last whitespace-separated token is the steps and the rest the track name (case-insensitive), and every track without a valid line is cleared; bad lines are skipped and listed as 'Line 2: unknown track Cymbal', 'Line 4: expected 16 steps' or 'Line 5: invalid step character' (line numbers count every pasted line).

Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo step edits, Euclid, Paste and Import (at least 50 steps). Patterns, chain, BPM and swing persist in localStorage.

Visual direction: hardware-inspired: a dark graphite body, rounded square pads that light orange (brighter for accents), a monospaced LCD-style readout, clearly separated beat groups.
interaction_hints:
Find the step pads from a screenshot or the DOM (row = track in the listed order, column = step 1-16) and click them; for Shift+click use keydown Shift, click, keyup Shift. Read the pattern header, the readout and the song line with eval of document.body.innerText or from screenshots. Before pressing the period, comma or Home keys, click an empty non-input area so no text field has focus. Every scenario starts from a fresh load. (1) Screenshot pattern A; click tab B and C and read their headers. (2) Press . 5 times and read the readout; press Home, press . 20 times, read; press . 17 more times (37 total), read; press Home then , once and read. (3) Set BPM to 90 and Swing to 66 (type with a selector, then press Tab or Enter), click an empty area, press Home and . 5 times, read the readout and the song line; then set BPM 120 and Swing 50 and read step 6 again (0:00.625). (4) Click Kick step 3 and read the header; fresh load: Shift+click Snare step 5 and read the header. (5) Open the Open hat Euclid control, set Hits 5 and Rotate 2, apply, look at the row and header. (6) Undo chain in ONE call: click Kick step 3; Euclid Open hat 5 / 2; Import the text 'kick x...x...x...x...
Cymbal x...............
Closed hat   xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Snare ....X.......X..x...
Rim ..X...........X.' (
 are newlines) and read the messages, the rows and the header; press Control+z three times reading the header after each; press Control+Shift+z three times and read. (7) Open Export on pattern A and read the text. Press Space, wait 1500 ms, screenshot (timeline block and readout moved), press Space again. (8) Click Copy pattern, click tab C, click Paste, read the header; set the chain to 'A C' and read the song line and timeline; set it to 'A E' and read the message. (9) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make changes (a step, the chain, BPM), then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and read again.

rubric.criterion: The layout has Play/Stop, BPM 120, Swing 60% and the position readout; tabs A, B, C and D; eight named tracks (Kick to Cowbell) with 16 pads grouped visibly in fours and a Euclid control per track; the chain field 'A A B A' with a timeline of four blocks labeled A, A, B, A; 'Song: 4 bars · 0:08.000'; and Export and Import controls.

Pattern A shows exactly the seeded steps (accents visibly stronger) with the header 'Pattern A · 19 hits · 5 accents'; tab B shows its seed with 'Pattern B · 22 hits · 5 accents'; tab C is empty with 0 hits and 0 accents.

Stepping with the period key from the start reads 'Bar 1 · A · Step 6 · 0:00.650' after 5 presses, 'Bar 2 · A · Step 5 · 0:02.500' after 20 and 'Bar 3 · B · Step 6 · 0:04.650' after 37; one comma press from the start wraps to 'Bar 4 · A · Step 16 · 0:07.900'.
With BPM 90 and Swing 66%, step 6 of bar 1 reads 0:00.887 and the song line reads 'Song: 4 bars · 0:10.667'; with BPM 120 and Swing 50% step 6 reads 0:00.625.

Clicking Kick step 3 makes the header 'Pattern A · 20 hits · 5 accents'; from a fresh load, Shift+clicking the accented Snare step 5 turns it into a normal hit and the header reads 19 hits and 4 accents.
Euclid on Open hat with Hits 5 and Rotate 2 sets the row to ..x...x..x..x..x (steps 3, 7, 10, 13 and 16 on) and the header to 23 hits and 5 accents.

Importing the five-line text from the hints lists 'Line 2: unknown track Cymbal' and 'Line 4: expected 16 steps', sets Kick to x...x...x...x..., all 16 Closed hat steps on and Rim accents on steps 3 and 15, clears every other row including Snare, and the header reads 22 hits and 2 accents.

Undo and redo span different operations: after clicking Kick step 3, the Euclid change and the import, Ctrl+Z three times shows 24/5, then 20/5, then 19/5 hits/accents, and Ctrl+Shift+Z three times returns to 22 hits and 2 accents.

Export of pattern A shows exactly eight lines in track order, from 'Kick X.....x...X..x..' to 'Cowbell ................' (with 'Closed hat x.x.x.x.x.x.x.xX'); Space starts playback so the readout and the highlighted timeline block advance, and Space stops it.
Copy pattern then Paste on tab C makes C read 19 hits and 5 accents; the chain 'A C' gives two timeline blocks and 'Song: 2 bars · 0:04.000'; the chain 'A E' shows 'Use A, B, C or D'.
After edits to steps, the chain and BPM, reloading the page restores the patterns, chain and tempo.

It looks like polished drum-machine hardware: dark graphite surfaces, rounded pads that glow orange with brighter accents, an LCD-style monospaced readout, clear beat grouping and aligned track labels.

title: Crossword constructor with live numbering, symmetric blocks and grid health
prompt:
Build Gridsmith, a crossword construction tool for 13×13 American-style grids.

The provided grid.json is the puzzle I am building: copy it into the output folder next to index.html and, when nothing is saved yet, load it at runtime with fetch('grid.json'); never hard-code it. It has a title, a size, 13 row strings ('#' block, '.' empty white cell, a letter for a filled cell) and clues for across and down keyed by the entry's start cell as 'row,col' (0-based).

Grid: 40×40 px cells, black blocks, letters centered, and standard numbering in the top-left corner: scanning rows top to bottom and left to right, a white cell gets the next number when it starts an across entry (a block or the edge on its left and a white cell on its right) or a down entry (the same vertically). An entry is a run of two or more white cells.

Selection and typing: clicking a white cell selects it (the direction starts as Across); clicking it again or pressing Space switches between Across and Down. The selected cell and its current entry are highlighted in the grid and in the clue list. Typing a letter fills the cell and moves to the next cell of the entry (it stays on the last cell). Backspace clears the cell, or if it is already empty moves back one cell in the entry and clears that. Arrow keys move to the next white cell in that direction. Tab and Shift+Tab go to the next and previous entry in clue order (all Across, then all Down).

Blocks: the period key or a right-click toggles the selected cell between white and block (a letter in it is removed). A Symmetry switch, on by default, toggles the cell rotated 180° around the center at the same time.

Clue lists: Across and Down, each item showing the number, the clue text (click to edit), and the letters as a pattern with underscores for empty cells (like AT_M). Clues stay with their entry's start cell when numbers change.

Health: a stats bar reads like 'Words 60 · Blocks 28 · Avg length 4.70 · Letters 10/141' (entries, blocks, the mean entry length with two decimals, filled cells over white cells). A warnings panel lists 'Unchecked cells: N' (white cells not in both an across and a down entry), 'Two-letter words: N' and 'Not symmetric' when they apply, or 'No warnings'.

History: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo letters (one step per letter), block toggles (a symmetric pair is one step, and undo brings back any removed letters) and clue edits. Export shows the puzzle as JSON in the grid.json format. Everything is saved to localStorage and restored after a reload.

Visual direction: a newspaper-grade construction tool: crisp black blocks and thin gray rules, small numbers, a pale yellow highlight for the current entry with a stronger selected cell, serif clue lists in two columns beside the grid, and a quiet sidebar for stats and warnings.
interaction_hints: The input file is /grader/task/grid.json; grep the page's JS for a relative fetch of grid.json (a hard-coded grid fails R2). Find the grid's top-left with eval (getBoundingClientRect of the grid element); the center of cell (row r, column c), 0-based, is at origin + (40c + 20, 40r + 20). prompt:
Build Huebench, a color palette studio for UI designers. Write the color math yourself; do not use a color library.

The palette has a title (start with 'Product UI') and five swatches in this order: Primary #2563EB, Secondary #0D9488, Accent #F59E0B, Neutral #64748B and Danger #DC2626. Each swatch shows a large color block, a hex field, H, S and L fields and a lock toggle.

Color rules:
- The hex value is the source of truth, shown uppercase like #2563EB. The hex field accepts 3 or 6 hex digits with or without '#' in any case (e11 means #EE1111) and applies on Enter or blur; anything else shows 'Use a hex color like #1A2B3C' under the field and keeps the old color.
- The H, S and L fields show the hex as HSL in whole numbers (H 0–359, S and L in percent). Editing one and pressing Enter sets the hex from the three whole numbers, rounding each RGB channel to the nearest integer (halves up); out-of-range values are clamped.
- Each swatch has a ten-step scale 50, 100, 200 … 900 built from its H and S fields with L set to 97, 93, 85, 75, 63, 52, 43, 35, 27 and 20; every step shows its number and hex.

Contrast matrix: rows are the five swatches as text; columns are White, Black and the five swatches as backgrounds. Each cell shows 'Aa' in the text color on the background, the WCAG 2 contrast ratio from relative luminance truncated (not rounded) to two decimals, and a badge from the exact ratio: AAA from 7, AA from 4.5, AA Large from 3, otherwise Fail. Diagonal cells are empty. Clicking a cell shows its details with a 'Fix for AA' button when the ratio is below 4.5. Fix for AA changes the text swatch's L by 1 at a time, keeping its H and S, darker when the background has the higher luminance and lighter otherwise, until the ratio reaches 4.5; if L runs out first it shows 'Cannot reach AA by changing lightness' and changes nothing. A locked text swatch is never changed: show 'Unlock Accent to fix it' with that swatch's name.

Harmony: a menu with Analogous (Secondary = Primary's hue + 30°, Accent = hue − 30°), Complementary (Secondary = hue + 180°) and Triadic (Secondary + 120°, Accent + 240°), all with Primary's S and L. Locked swatches, Neutral and Danger never change.

Import: a dialog where I can paste GIMP palette text or pick a .gpl file; harbor.gpl is a sample. The first line must be 'GIMP Palette'; 'Name:' sets the palette title; 'Columns:', '#' comments and blank lines are ignored; other lines must be R G B values from 0 to 255 plus an optional name, and any other line is skipped. The colors fill the unlocked swatches in order (extra colors are ignored) and a notice reads like 'Read 6 colors · 1 line skipped (line 9)'.

Export CSS opens a dialog with '/* <title> */', then ':root {', then for each swatch in order its base like '  --primary: #2563eb;' followed by '  --primary-50: …;' through '  --primary-900: …;' (two-space indent, lowercase hex), then '}'.

Every color change (hex or HSL edit, harmony, Fix for AA, import with its title) is one undo step: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z and toolbar buttons undo and redo it; locking is not a step. The URL hash always holds the colors like '#p=2563eb,0d9488,f59e0b,64748b,dc2626', and opening the page with such a hash, or changing it, loads those colors. The title, colors and locks persist in localStorage; a hash present on load wins.

Visual direction: a precise designer tool: a near-white neutral UI so the colors stand out, monospace hex and ratio values, badges green for AAA and AA, amber for AA Large and red for Fail, a clear lock state, and scale steps whose labels switch between dark and light text to stay readable.
interaction_hints: Fields: type with a selector, then press Enter. Read values from screenshots and with eval of the DOM text. Matrix cells: rows are the text swatch, columns the background (White, Black, then the swatches); find a cell from a screenshot. Suggested calls from a fresh load each: (1) screenshot; read every hex and HSL field, the scales (Primary 50/500/900, Accent 100/600, Danger 700, Neutral 300) and the matrix cells named in R3. (2) Danger hex: type e11, Enter; read its hex, HSL and the Danger/White cell. Primary hex: type zz1234, Enter; read the message and Primary's hex. Primary L field: type 45, Enter; read Primary's hex and the Primary/White cell. (3) Click the Secondary/White cell and Fix for AA; click Accent/White and Fix for AA; click Danger/Neutral and Fix for AA; read hexes, cells and messages. Then lock Accent (fresh load or after undo) and try Fix for AA on Accent/White. (4) Lock Accent, apply Analogous; read Secondary and Accent. Unlock Accent, apply Triadic; read Secondary, Accent, Neutral and Danger. (5) Lock Neutral, open Import, type the full text of /grader/task/harbor.gpl into the textarea (type with its selector; tabs and newlines are fine), apply; read the notice, title, five hexes, the Primary/White and Accent/Primary cells; press Control+z and check the seed colors and 'Product UI' return. (6) Open Export CSS; eval the dialog text: line count, first four lines, the --secondary-500, --accent-700 and last lines. (7) Primary L 45 + Enter, apply Triadic, then press Control+z, screenshot, Control+z, screenshot, Control+Shift+z, screenshot. (8) Hash: after an edit eval location.hash; then eval "location.hash = '#p=0f4c81,2a9d8f,e9c46a,264653,e76f51'", wait 800 ms and read the swatches. (9) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: change a color and lock a swatch, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and read again.

rubric.criterion: Five swatches Primary, Secondary, Accent, Neutral and Danger show hex #2563EB, #0D9488, #F59E0B, #64748B, #DC2626 with HSL fields 221/83/53, 175/84/32, 38/92/50, 215/16/47 and 0/72/51, each with a lock toggle; the title reads 'Product UI'.
Each swatch has a labeled 50–900 scale with exact hexes, including Primary 50 #F1F5FE, 500 #1F5FEA, 900 #09235D; Accent 100 #FEF2DD, 600 #D38909; Danger 700 #9A1919; Neutral 300 #B5BEC9.

The matrix has five text rows and seven background columns (White, Black, the swatches) with empty diagonal cells; on load it reads Primary/White 5.16 AA, Secondary/White 3.74 AA Large, Accent/White 2.14 Fail, Accent/Black 9.77 AAA, Neutral/White 4.75 AA, Danger/Black 4.34 AA Large and Primary on Secondary 1.38 Fail (truncated, so 5.17, 2.15 or 4.76 fail this item).

Typing e11 in Danger's hex gives #EE1111 with HSL 0/87/50 and Danger/White 4.44 AA Large; zz1234 in Primary's hex shows 'Use a hex color like #1A2B3C' and keeps #2563EB; setting Primary's L to 45 gives #1450D2 with Primary/White 6.75 AA.

Fix for AA on Secondary over White makes Secondary #0B8379 at 4.62 AA; on Accent over White makes Accent #A26907 at 4.60 AA; on Danger over Neutral shows 'Cannot reach AA by changing lightness' and keeps #DC2626; with Accent locked it shows 'Unlock Accent to fix it' and keeps #F59E0B.
With Accent locked, Analogous sets Secondary to #4824EB and keeps Accent #F59E0B; with nothing locked, Triadic sets Secondary #EB2463 and Accent #63EB24; Neutral and Danger never change.

With Neutral locked, importing harbor.gpl shows 'Read 6 colors · 1 line skipped (line 9)', the title 'Harbor' and swatches #0F4C81, #2A9D8F, #E9C46A, #64748B (kept) and #F4A261, with Primary/White 8.85 AAA and Accent on Primary 5.30 AA; Ctrl+Z restores the previous colors and title.

Export CSS on load shows 58 lines: '/* Product UI */', ':root {', '  --primary: #2563eb;', '  --primary-50: #f1f5fe;' … including '  --secondary-500: #1eebda;' and '  --accent-700: #ab6f07;', ending with '  --danger-900: #580e0e;' and '}'.

After setting Primary's L to 45 and applying Triadic, Ctrl+Z restores Secondary #0D9488 and Accent #F59E0B, a second Ctrl+Z restores Primary #2563EB, and Ctrl+Shift+Z re-applies #1450D2, with the scales and matrix following each step.

The hash follows the palette (after the L 45 edit it reads '#p=1450d2,0d9488,f59e0b,64748b,dc2626'); setting the hash to '#p=0f4c81,2a9d8f,e9c46a,264653,e76f51' loads #0F4C81, #2A9D8F, #E9C46A, #264653 and #E76F51; colors and locks survive a reload.
At 1280×800 the swatch columns, their scales and the contrast matrix are aligned without overlap or clipping; every scale step's number and hex is readable on its own color.

A polished designer tool: near-white neutral chrome, consistent spacing and radii, monospace hex and ratio values, badges green for AAA/AA, amber for AA Large and red for Fail, and an obvious locked state.

title: Document viewer with search, outline, highlights, notes and JSON round-trip
prompt:
Build Folio, a document viewer for our annual report. The provided report.json holds the document: an id, a title and pages, each page a list of blocks with a type (h1, h2 or p) and text. Copy it next to index.html and load it at runtime with fetch('report.json'); never hard-code its text. If it cannot be loaded, show an error card reading 'Could not open report.json'.

Layout: a toolbar with the document title, page navigation, zoom and search; a left sidebar with Thumbnails, Outline and 'Annotations (N)' tabs; and a gray scrolling viewer showing every page as a white sheet, 816×1056 px at 100%, with a shadow, a small running header with the document title and the page number at the bottom.

Navigation: a 'Page [3] of 7' field: typing a number and pressing Enter scrolls that page's top to the top of the viewer; out-of-range numbers revert. J or PageDown goes to the next page and K or PageUp to the previous one when no field has focus. The current page is the one under the vertical middle of the viewer; the field and the highlighted thumbnail follow scrolling. Thumbnails are miniature pages with numbers; clicking one goes there. The outline lists the h1 headings with the following h2 headings nested under them; clicking an entry scrolls to that heading.

Zoom: − and + buttons and a menu with 50%, 75%, 100%, 125%, 150%, 200% and Fit width (the sheet 48 px narrower than the viewer). It opens at 100%. The sheet and its text scale together and the current page stays in view.

Search: Ctrl+F focuses the search field. As I type, every match in the block text of all pages (headings included, running headers not; non-overlapping, never across blocks) gets a yellow highlight, the first becomes current in orange and scrolls to the middle of the viewer, and a label reads like 'Match 1 of 17'. Enter and Shift+Enter step forward and back in document order and wrap around; 'No results' when nothing matches. Matching ignores case unless the Aa toggle is on; the whole-word toggle keeps only matches with no letter or digit right before or after. Escape clears the search.

Annotations:
- Select text inside a block and press H or click Highlight to mark it in the current color (Yellow, Green or Pink in the toolbar; Yellow by default); surrounding spaces are left out.
- The Note tool (button or N) places a numbered sticky note where I click on a page and opens a text box; Enter saves, Escape cancels.
- The Annotations tab groups them by page under headers like 'Page 2 · 2 annotations' ('1 annotation' for one), showing each highlight's text or the note's text with its color; clicking one scrolls to it; each has a delete button, and Delete removes a selected one.
- Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo adding, deleting and importing annotations.
- Export shows JSON with a document field holding the document id and an annotations array sorted by page, highlights (by block, then start) before notes. A highlight has type 'highlight', page (from 1), block (index in the page, from 0), start and end (character offsets in the block text, end exclusive), color ('yellow', 'green' or 'pink') and text; a note has type 'note', page, x and y (fractions of the page width and height, 3 decimals) and text.
- Import takes such JSON pasted into a dialog and replaces all annotations. Another document id is refused with 'This file belongs to another document'; entries with an unknown page or block, offsets outside the block, start not before end or an unknown color are skipped, and a notice reads like 'Imported 2 annotations · 1 skipped'. Imported highlights take their text from the offsets.

Annotations, the zoom and the current page persist in localStorage under the key 'folio:' plus the document id and are restored after a reload.

Visual direction: a calm reading app in the spirit of Preview or Acrobat: a medium-gray canvas, crisp white sheets with soft shadows, a serif for the document text with a clear h1/h2/body hierarchy, a sans-serif UI, one blue accent, and highlights that keep the text readable.
interaction_hints: The input file is /grader/task/report.json; grep the page's HTML/JS for a relative fetch of report.json (hard-coded text fails R1). Measure sheets with eval (getBoundingClientRect of the page elements). Press single-letter keys only after clicking an empty part of the gray viewer so no field has focus. To double-click a word: bring its page into view (page field), then with eval walk the text nodes, build a Range around the word and return its getBoundingClientRect center, and dblclick those coordinates. Suggested calls from a fresh load each: (1) screenshot; eval the number and size of the sheets; open Outline, screenshot, click 'Capital program' and read the page field. (2) type 6 into the page field with its selector, press Enter, screenshot; click the gray viewer background, press j, then k; type 9 + Enter in the field and read it; click thumbnail 2. (3) choose 150% and measure a sheet; 50%; Fit width (compare with the viewer's width); go to page 5, choose 150% and read the page field. (4) press Control+f, type water, read the label; toggle Aa, read; toggle Aa off and whole word on, read; repeat for rate and district (all four combinations) and desalination. (5) search water, press Enter 10 times, screenshot, read the label and the page field; clear and type water again, press Shift+Enter; press Escape and check the highlights are gone. (6) dblclick 'turbidity' on page 2, press h; choose Green, dblclick 'acoustic' on page 3, press h; open the Annotations tab and screenshot. (7) click Note (or press n), click inside page 5, type Check call volumes, press Enter; click that item in the Annotations tab and read the page field. (8) after (6), delete the turbidity item, press Control+z, then Control+Shift+z, screenshotting each step. (9) after (6), open Export and read the JSON; open Import, type this into the textarea with its selector and apply: {"document":"nwa-ar-2025","annotations":[{"type":"highlight","page":3,"block":2,"start":0,"end":22,"color":"green","text":"x"},{"type":"note","page":4,"x":0.5,"y":0.3,"text":"Verify figure"},{"type":"highlight","page":9,"block":0,"start":0,"end":5,"color":"yellow","text":"x"}]} ; read the notice and the Annotations tab and check the green highlight covers exactly 'Non-revenue water fell' on page 3; then import {"document":"other","annotations":[]} and read the message. (10) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: add a highlight, zoom to 125% and go to page 4, eval Object.keys(localStorage), then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot. (11) Missing file: copy /grader/artifact to /tmp/nodoc, delete report.json there and run interact with --artifact-dir /tmp/nodoc.

rubric.criterion: report.json is in the output folder and loaded at runtime with a relative fetch (no hard-coded text); all 7 pages render in order as white sheets 816×1056 px at 100% (within 2 px) with a running header and page numbers; the toolbar shows 'Page 1 of 7' and the sidebar has Thumbnails, Outline and Annotations tabs.

The outline nests: 2025 Annual Report › Letter from the Chair; Operations › Water supply, Treatment, Distribution network, Metering; Finance › Revenue and rates, Capital program; Customers and Community › Customer service, Education and outreach; Sustainability › Energy and emissions, Watershed protection; Outlook for 2026 › Board of Directors. Clicking 'Capital program' scrolls to it and the field reads 'Page 4 of 7'.

Entering 6 in the page field puts page 6 at the top with 'Page 6 of 7' and thumbnail 6 highlighted; J then goes to page 7 and K back to 6; entering 9 reverts the field to 6; clicking thumbnail 2 goes to page 2.

At 150% the sheets are 1224 px wide and at 50% 408 px (within 2 px) with the text scaled along; Fit width makes a sheet about 48 px narrower than the viewer's visible width; going to page 5 and zooming to 150% keeps 'Page 5 of 7'.

Search counts: 'water' gives 'Match 1 of 17', 10 with Aa, 14 with whole word; 'rate' 17 and 9 with whole word; 'district' 3, 2 with Aa, 2 with whole word and 1 with both; 'desalination' shows 'No results'.

For 'water', pressing Enter ten times shows 'Match 11 of 17' with the orange current match on page 4 and the field at 'Page 4 of 7'; Shift+Enter from the first match wraps to 'Match 17 of 17' on page 7; Escape removes all search highlights.

Double-clicking 'turbidity' on page 2 and pressing H adds a yellow highlight on exactly that word, and the tab reads 'Annotations (1)' with 'Page 2 · 1 annotation' and 'turbidity'; choosing Green and highlighting 'acoustic' on page 3 adds a green one under 'Page 3 · 1 annotation' and 'Annotations (2)'.
The Note tool places a numbered note where clicked on page 5; typing 'Check call volumes' and Enter saves it; it is listed under page 5 and clicking the list item brings page 5 into view.
With both highlights, deleting 'turbidity' removes it from the page and the list ('Annotations (1)'); Ctrl+Z restores it and Ctrl+Shift+Z deletes it again.

Export shows document 'nwa-ar-2025' and the turbidity highlight as type 'highlight', page 2, block 5, start 98, end 107, color 'yellow', text 'turbidity'. Importing the three-entry test JSON shows 'Imported 2 annotations · 1 skipped' and replaces the annotations with a green highlight on exactly 'Non-revenue water fell' on page 3 and the note 'Verify figure' on page 4; a JSON for document 'other' is refused with 'This file belongs to another document'.
Annotations, the zoom level and the current page survive a reload, stored under the localStorage key 'folio:nwa-ar-2025'; with report.json missing the page shows 'Could not open report.json'.

A polished reading app: medium-gray canvas, crisp white sheets with soft shadows, a serif document font with clear h1/h2/body hierarchy, a tidy sans-serif toolbar and sidebar with one blue accent, and highlights that keep the text readable.

title: Flowchart editor with snapping connectors, live validation and JSON/SVG round-trip
prompt:
Build Flowline, a flowchart editor drawn with SVG (no diagram or canvas library).

Layout: a toolbar (Undo, Redo, Import JSON, Export JSON, Export SVG), a left palette (Start, End, Process, Decision), a canvas with a 20 px grid, a right panel with the Inspector above an Issues panel, and a status line like 'Nodes 4 · Connectors 3'.

Shapes are 140 px wide: Start and End are 40 px tall pills, Process a 60 px tall rectangle and Decision an 80 px tall diamond, each with a centered label and four ports at the middles of its sides. Clicking a palette item adds that shape, labeled with its type name, at X 320, Y 40; dragging it onto the canvas drops it where released. New ids continue the numbering (n11, e11).

Grid: X and Y are a shape's top-left corner in canvas pixels. Whenever a shape is placed, dragged or typed into the Inspector, both snap to the nearest multiple of 20, halves rounding up (233 becomes 240, 50 becomes 60). Arrow keys move the selection by 20 px.

Connectors: drag from a port (shown on hover) and release over another shape to connect to its port nearest the release point. Connectors are arrows of horizontal and vertical segments only, stay attached to their ports and re-route when shapes move. Double-click one to edit its label.

Selection: click, Shift+click to add or remove, and a marquee drag on empty canvas selects the shapes entirely inside it. Delete removes the selected shapes with every connector touching them, or a selected connector; Escape deselects. The Inspector edits the selected shape's Label, X and Y.

Issues: a panel titled 'Issues (N)' lists every problem, updated after every change, in these groups and this order: 'Missing Start node' or 'More than one Start node'; 'Missing End node' or 'More than one End node'; 'Unreachable: <label>' for every shape that cannot be reached from the Start by following arrows (checked only when there is exactly one Start); 'Decision <label> needs 2 labeled exits' unless it has exactly two outgoing connectors, both labeled; and 'Dead end: <label>' for every shape other than an End without an outgoing connector. Within a group, shapes follow document order (file order, then creation order). With no problems it reads 'Flowchart is valid'.

Data: when nothing is autosaved, import flowchart.json (copy it next to index.html and fetch it at runtime); if it cannot be loaded, show 'Could not load flowchart.json' and start empty. Its format is {name, nodes: [{id, type, label, x, y}], edges: [{id, from, fromPort, to, toPort, label}]} with types start, end, process, decision and ports top, right, bottom, left. Export JSON shows the diagram in exactly this format; Import JSON replaces it from pasted text, and invalid input shows a message starting 'Invalid flowchart' and changes nothing. Export SVG shows standalone SVG markup without the grid, its viewBox fitted to the shapes plus a 20 px margin.

History: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo every change (add, move, connect, label, delete, import), one step per drag or key press, at least 50 steps. The diagram autosaves to localStorage and is restored after a reload.

Visual direction: a clean diagramming tool in the spirit of Whimsical: white canvas with a faint grid, soft fills per type (green Start and End, blue Process, amber Decision), 1.5 px slate outlines and arrows, a blue selection outline with visible ports, and a compact side panel.
interaction_hints: The input file is /grader/task/flowchart.json; grep the page's JS for a relative fetch of flowchart.json (hard-coded shapes fail R2). Shapes can usually be clicked by their label text (selector text=Refund). For coordinates, eval the getBoundingClientRect of the canvas svg and add a shape's X/Y from the Inspector (check the mapping by clicking a label first). Shape sizes: 140 wide, 40/60/80 tall; ports sit at side midpoints. Use drag with steps 20 or more; for Shift+click use keydown Shift, click, keyup Shift. Type into Inspector fields with a selector, then press Enter. Suggested calls from a fresh load each: (1) screenshot; read the status line and the Issues panel. (2) Click Refund; set X to 587 and press Enter, set Y to 50 and press Enter; read X and Y (580, 60); press ArrowDown and read Y (80); screenshot its connector to Notify customer. (3) Drag Ship order by its body to another spot; read X and Y (multiples of 20) and look at its two connectors. (4) Double-click the unlabeled connector from In stock? to Backorder (on its horizontal segment), type No, press Enter; read Issues. Hover Backorder, drag from its top port (canvas point 630,460) onto Notify customer; read the status line and Issues. Click Refund, press Delete; read. Press Control+z and read; press Control+z twice more and read; press Control+Shift+z and read. (5) Click Check stock, press Delete; read the status line and all Issues in order. Separately, click Start in the palette and read Issues. (6) Shift+click Refund and Backorder (or marquee-drag on empty canvas from canvas point 540,100 to 720,540), press Delete; read. (7) Export JSON and read it (10 nodes, 10 edges, file ids and coordinates); Export SVG and read the viewBox; Import JSON with the exported text but Ship order renamed to Ship parcel; then Import JSON with the text {oops. (8) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make changes (move a shape, add a connector), then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot or eval again. (9) Missing file: copy /grader/artifact to /tmp/noflow, delete flowchart.json there and run interact with --artifact-dir /tmp/noflow.

rubric.criterion: The layout has the toolbar (Undo, Redo, Import JSON, Export JSON, Export SVG), a palette with Start, End, Process and Decision, a gridded SVG canvas, the Inspector and Issues panels and the status line; with flowchart.json missing the page shows 'Could not load flowchart.json', an empty canvas and exactly the issues 'Missing Start node' and 'Missing End node'.

flowchart.json is loaded at runtime with a relative fetch and drawn as 10 shapes at their file positions: pills for Order received and Done, diamonds for Payment OK? and In stock?, rectangles for the other six; 10 arrow connectors with the labels Yes and No out of Payment OK? and Yes out of In stock?; the status line reads 'Nodes 10 · Connectors 10'.
On load the Issues panel reads 'Issues (3)' with exactly 'Unreachable: Refund', 'Decision In stock? needs 2 labeled exits' and 'Dead end: Backorder' in that order.

With Refund selected, typing X 587 and Y 50 in the Inspector puts it at X 580, Y 60; ArrowDown then shows Y 80; the Refund to Notify customer connector stays attached and is made only of horizontal and vertical segments.

Dragging a shape moves it to a position whose X and Y are multiples of 20 (as shown in the Inspector), and every connector attached to it follows and re-routes with only horizontal and vertical segments.

Double-clicking the unlabeled In stock? to Backorder connector and entering No leaves 'Issues (2)' (Unreachable: Refund, Dead end: Backorder); dragging from a Backorder port onto Notify customer adds an arrow, the status line reads 'Nodes 10 · Connectors 11' and only 'Unreachable: Refund' remains.

Continuing, deleting Refund gives 'Nodes 9 · Connectors 10' and 'Flowchart is valid'; Ctrl+Z restores Refund with its connector (Nodes 10 · Connectors 11, Issues (1)); two more Ctrl+Z remove the new connector and the No label (Issues (3) again); Ctrl+Shift+Z re-applies the label.

From a fresh load, deleting Check stock also removes its two connectors ('Nodes 9 · Connectors 8') and the panel reads 'Issues (7)': Unreachable: In stock?, Unreachable: Ship order, Unreachable: Refund, Unreachable: Backorder, Decision Payment OK? needs 2 labeled exits, Decision In stock? needs 2 labeled exits, Dead end: Backorder. Separately, clicking Start in the palette adds a Start shape at X 320, Y 40 and the panel reads 'Issues (4)' starting with 'More than one Start node' and ending with 'Dead end: Start'.

Selecting Refund and Backorder together (Shift+click or a marquee around both) and pressing Delete removes both with their connectors: 'Nodes 8 · Connectors 8' and 'Issues (1)' with only 'Decision In stock? needs 2 labeled exits'.

Export JSON right after load shows the file format with the same 10 nodes and 10 edges (same ids, types, labels, coordinates, ports and labels) and reflects a moved shape's new x and y; importing edited JSON updates the canvas (a renamed shape shows its new label) and invalid text shows a message starting 'Invalid flowchart' without changing the diagram; Export SVG markup has viewBox '40 20 680 620'.
After moving a shape and adding a connector, reloading the page restores the diagram with the same positions, connectors and labels instead of re-importing the file.

A polished diagramming look: faint grid, distinct fills per shape type, crisp labels centered in their shapes, arrowheads that end exactly at the ports, a clear blue selection outline with ports, and an aligned, compact side panel.

title: Text diff and three-way merge tool with word highlights, conflicts and undo
prompt:
Build Mergewise, a text diff and three-way merge tool for config files.

Files: copy base.txt, ours.txt and theirs.txt next to index.html and load them at runtime with fetch; never hard-code their text. If one cannot be loaded, show an error card naming it, like 'Could not load theirs.txt'.

Compare view (#/compare/<left>/<right>, default #/compare/base/ours): Left and Right selectors choose among Base, Ours and Theirs and update the hash, and opening such a URL directly shows that pair.
- Use a minimal line diff (a longest common subsequence of lines). Stats read like '+3 −2' (added and removed lines). A hunk is a maximal run of consecutive changed lines.
- Side-by-side mode: old on the left and new on the right with line numbers on both sides, removed lines red and added lines green. Within a hunk, removed and added lines are paired in order on shared rows; unpaired lines face an empty filler.
- Unified mode: one column with both line-number gutters and '-' or '+' prefixes; unchanged lines stay visible.
- Word highlights: in each paired row, split both lines into words (letters, digits and underscores), runs of spaces and single other characters, and highlight only the tokens outside their longest common subsequence.
- 'Ignore whitespace' compares lines with leading and trailing spaces or tabs removed and inner runs collapsed to one space; stats, hunks and colors follow it.
- The toolbar shows 'Hunk 1 of N'; the n and p keys move to the next or previous hunk (stopping at the ends), outline it and scroll it into view.

Merge view (#/merge): a three-way merge of Ours and Theirs against Base, using each side's minimal diff from Base. A change made by one side only is applied automatically, the same change on both sides is applied once, and different changes by both sides to the same Base lines are a conflict. Show Ours and Theirs side by side (read-only, their changed lines tinted) above the Result, where each conflict is a block showing both versions with three buttons: Accept ours, Accept theirs and Accept both (ours first). The header reads 'Conflicts remaining: N' and 'Auto-merged: X from ours · Y from theirs · Z identical', counting hunks. Download merged (saving relay.merged.conf) stays disabled until no conflicts remain; then the Result becomes an editable text area with a footer like 'Merged: 40 lines' that follows edits (a final newline does not count as a line). Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo resolutions. Resolutions and edits persist in localStorage and survive a reload.

Visual direction: a developer tool in the spirit of GitHub's diff view: 13 px monospace code (DejaVu Sans Mono or Liberation Mono), a light theme, soft red and green line backgrounds with stronger word highlights, gray line-number gutters, amber conflict blocks and a compact toolbar with a segmented Side-by-side / Unified switch.

title: Round-robin league manager with head-to-head tie-breakers, what-if mode and CSV round-trip
prompt:
Build Fixtura, a league manager for the Riverside Sunday League 2026: six five-a-side teams playing a double round robin (10 rounds of 3 matches).

Teams in seeding order 1 to 6: Ashford Albion, Bramley Rovers, Cobalt City, Dockside United, Elmwood Athletic, Fenwick Town. A team's slug is its name in lower case with hyphens (cobalt-city).

Fixtures use the circle method. Start from the list [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. Each round pairs list positions 1 and 6, 2 and 5, then 3 and 4, in that order; the first team of each pair is at home, except that seed 1 plays away in even rounds. After each round seed 1 stays first and the others rotate: the last team moves to position 2 and the rest shift right, so round 2 uses [1, 6, 2, 3, 4, 5] (Elmwood Athletic v Ashford Albion, Fenwick Town v Dockside United, Bramley Rovers v Cobalt City). Rounds 6 to 10 repeat rounds 1 to 5 with home and away swapped.

Results: when nothing is saved, load results.csv (copy it next to index.html and fetch it at runtime; never hard-code its rows). Its header is round,home,away,home_goals,away_goals. A row is skipped when that home team does not host that away team in that round, a score is not a whole number from 0 to 99, or the match already has a result earlier in the file. Show a notice like 'Loaded 12 results · 2 rows skipped (lines 4, 9)' with file line numbers (the header is line 1), or just 'Loaded 12 results'. If the file is missing, show 'Could not load results.csv' and start with no results.

Table (#/table, the default): Pos, Team, P, W, D, L, GF, GA, GD, Pts and Form (the last five results as W, D or L chips, newest on the right). A win earns 3 points and a draw 1. Teams level on points are ordered by a mini-table of only the matches between all of the tied teams (points, then goal difference), then overall goal difference, goals for and name. Every team gets its own position.

Fixtures (#/fixtures): all rounds with two score inputs per match. Entering both scores and pressing Enter saves a result, clearing both removes it, and anything else shows 'Scores must be whole numbers from 0 to 99' and saves nothing. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo result changes, imports included.

What if: a switch that makes the inputs of unplayed matches record predictions, shown dashed and in another color. While it is on, the table is labeled 'Projected' and counts predictions; 'Discard predictions' or switching it off removes them. Predictions are never saved or exported.

Team pages (#/team/<slug>, opened by clicking a team name anywhere): position like '4th of 6', points, W-D-L, GF and GA, form, and the team's 10 fixtures in round order with scores and a W, D or L chip.

Export CSV shows the played results in the file format, in round and fixture order, with a Download button; Import CSV replaces all results from pasted text with the same validation and notice. Results persist in localStorage.
